The Master's ETA for Sept-Iles (2025-01-31T11:00:00Z) is consistent: the computed ETA from distance to go (1503.8 nm avoiding belle_isle) at 12.5 kn is 2025-01-31T12:18:00Z, within the 2-hour tolerance. No ETA notice is due now — the last notice was sent 5 days before arrival (ETA 2025-01-31T06:00:00Z, sent 2025-01-25T12:30:00Z) to the agent; the next threshold is 3 days.

The remarks explain the stop, so no query to the Master is needed. check_stoppage confirmed the main engine stoppage of 0610–1140 UTC on 26 Jan (5.5 hours) agrees with the report: 18.5 steaming hours at 12.5 kn gives the 231.3 nm distance run exactly, and the stop falls within the report day. VLSFO used during the stop: 1.1 t.

The off-hire statement figures are simulated: hire deducted $2,177.08 (5.5 h at $9,500/day), plus 1.1 t VLSFO at $660 charged to the owners' account, total $2,837.08. Under the CP off-hire clause, loss of time from breakdown of machinery preventing full working of the vessel puts hire off for the time lost, and bunkers used while off hire are for the owners' account — this stoppage appears to fall within that clause. Note the owner may argue the cause lies in the fuel supplied by the charterer; that claim is the operator's to make.

The operator should decide whether to put the ship off hire for the stop and notify the owner. If yes: (a) propose a voyage management system off-hire entry for 2025-01-26T06:10:00Z to 2025-01-26T11:40:00Z, and (b) email the owner's vessel technical management (Tormar Bulk Carriers) giving the period and reason and asking for the engine log extract for the stop.

Summary for the operator:

- No figures are missing from the report for the desk.

Simulated figures: hire deducted $2,177.08 (5.5 h at $9,500/day), plus 1.1 t VLSFO at $660 for owners' account — total $2,837.08.

draft.body:
Dear Owner,

Please note that MV TORMAR SPRING (SIM-0002) is put off hire for the main engine stoppage on 26 Jan 2025 from 0610 to 1140 UTC (5.5 hours).
